findings.title: Missing fd_select bounds check in CID incremental interface
findings.message: In cid_load_glyph(), when the incremental interface is active, fd_select is read directly from callback-supplied glyph data via cid_get_offset() without validating that it is less than cid->num_dicts. The unchecked value is subsequently used as an array index into face->subrs, allowing an attacker-controlled value to produce an out-of-bounds pointer that is then dereferenced, causing a heap-buffer-overflow read. The non-incremental path correctly validates fd_select against cid->num_dicts before use, but this check was omitted when the incremental code path was first introduced.
findings.suggestion: After reading fd_select from the callback-supplied glyph data, validate it against cid->num_dicts before using it as an array index. Mirror the existing check in the non-incremental code path. Additionally, handle the sentinel values 0xFF (fd_bytes==1) and 0xFFFF (fd_bytes==2) as empty-glyph indicators.

ground_truth.root_cause: When the incremental interface code path was first introduced in 2002, the bounds check that guards fd_select in the ordinary (non-incremental) code path was never added to the incremental branch. Both paths call cid_get_offset() to extract fd_select from untrusted data, but only the ordinary path validates the result before using it as an array index.
